citation.title: Topology Optimisation under Uncertainties with Neural Networks
citation.authors: Martin Eigel; Marvin Haase; Johannes Neumann

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The neural networks predict optimization gradient steps that permit larger steps and outperform the classical method in the 2D bridge benchmark.
claim.key_phrase: clearly outperforms the classical optimisation method
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Table 1, deterministic bridge at load (0, −5000)T: classical Algorithm A1 4 min 43 s (283 s) divided by CNN Algorithm 1 4 min 05 s (245 s) = 1.1551×.
claim.alternatives: The conclusion reports larger iteration steps; Table 4 reports mixed load-specific runtime and compliance results, while LSTM Algorithm 3 has longer computation time overall.

baseline.classical_method: Phase-field Allen–Cahn gradient optimization with adaptive mesh refinement (Algorithms A1/A2)
baseline.implementation: FEniCS finite-element simulation; Python/PyTorch for neural networks; repository publicly linked in Introduction
baseline.solver: finite-element state/adjoint equations; linear solver details not stated
baseline.problem_size: 2D bridge; maximum fine mesh |V(Tm)| ≤ 15,000 vertices (Section 4.1.3); Appendix A benchmark
baseline.classical_iterations: Convergence criterion in Equation (A1); deterministic load (0, −5000)T: 538 iterations (Table 1)
baseline.classical_time: 4 min 43 s for deterministic load (0, −5000)T (Table 1); Table 4 gives five-load results
baseline.ml_time: 4 min 05 s for CNN Algorithm 1 at (0, −5000)T (Table 1); LSTM Algorithm 3: 4 min 34 s
baseline.data_generation_cost: Training tuples generated from classical optimizer runs (Section 4.1.1); elapsed data-generation cost not stated
baseline.quality_gap: At (0, −5000)T, compliance 1173.22 classical vs 1148.66 CNN; objective 1475.39 vs 1206.49 (Table 1)

R1.evidence: Section 4.1.3 and Table 1: same bridge load and convergence criterion are compared; outputs are described as essentially identical, with compliance 1173.22 (classical) and 1148.66 (CNN).

R2.evidence: Section 4.1 and Table 1 compare FEniCS classical and PyTorch CNN workflows, but neither hardware nor solver configuration is stated.

R3.evidence: Section 4.1.1 describes generating training tuples with the classical optimizer, but no elapsed training or data-generation cost or amortization is reported.

R4.evidence: Sections 2 and 4 evaluate compliance using finite-element state equations and impose a volume constraint; Sections 4.1.4 and 4.4 discuss topology collapse for some cases but do not report a failure rate.

reporting.n_test_cases: Five applied loads in Table 4; deterministic timing averaged over 10 runs (Section 4.1.3); stochastic comparison uses 224 samples (Table 2)

notes: Public repository is linked in the Introduction; article is open access under CC BY. The primary comparison is qualitative in the abstract; the first quantitative runtime is in Table 1.
